items.summary: The busy training base is located behind fences on remote land in Alberta A huge fire swept through a Canadian military base on Saturday, killing at least four people and seriously injuring dozens more Prime Minister Mark Carney described it as one of the worst peace time tragedies on Canadian soil in the history of the military Here is what we know about the deadly incident so far Few details about what triggered the deadly fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, which broke out at around 16:00 local time (22:00 GMT), have been confirmed by authorities so far Local media reported it may have been started when a gas main was struck during a live firing exercise taking place on the grounds Carney said a "violent, fast-moving fire swept through the base" without confirming what started it Minister of National Defence David McGuinty said those caught up in the fire were "training on the range" The Municipal District of Wainwright posted on social media that the fire had "spread rapidly due to high winds" The prime minister said military and civilian fire crews "fought this fire…

items.title: Inside Chicago's battle against the synthetic drugs flooding the US
items.summary: Warning: This video contains descriptions of drug-taking and distressing images A new wave of synthetic drugs is sweeping across the United States, raising fear of a worsening drug crisis Earlier this year, President Donald Trump pledged a crackdown on drug cartels, proscribing many as terrorist organisations Drug overdose deaths have fallen from a peak of around 110,000 in 2022, down to roughly 70,000 last year However, America's decades-long drug crisis may be accelerating and authorities are increasingly concerned about cheaper, more powerful synthetic drugs, including an animal tranquilliser called tranq The BBC's Quentin Sommerville reports from the frontlines in South Side, Chicago, where communities are battling the crisis

items.title: Albania's Prime Minister Edi Rama ignores calls to resign amid violent clashes
items.summary: Anti-government protesters continued calls for Edi Rama to step down as violent clashes between demonstrators and police again took place Student-led protests continued in Albania for a sixth day with continued demands for Prime Minister Edi Rama to resign Despite those calls, Rama is refusing to step down , saying the demonstrations were not a threat to government but rather a threat to Albania's ambition of accession to the European Union "I ​am not being challenged, the government is not being challenged, a government majority or a winning party in the elections is not being challenged but a path is being challenged, a mission is being challenged," Rama said in a live address on Facebook "Albanians need to think ​very clearly: Do they want this, do they want that, or do they want the EU?” Rama asked Rama ruled out resigning and said that the protests are the "work of an outside hand." Earlier in the week Rama ruled out resigning, saying that governments were changed through elections Student-led demonstrations, spurred by discontent over alleged government corruption…

items.title: Mozambique: ANE awards 20.6 billion meticais for Inhambane and Sofala road contracts
items.summary: According to the contract award notices published by ANE’s provincial delegations, the contracts concern new lots for road engineering and paving projects, five of which are located in Inhambane province, in southern Mozambique, and four in Sofala, in the centre of the country The awards fall under the 2026–2031 Accelerated National Road Rehabilitation and Construction Programme, known as “More Roads – 2031”, and cover national and regional road links In Inhambane province, the contracts total 285 kilometres and 10,104,807,009 meticais (€143.6 million) The contracts were awarded to a consortium comprising the companies Maripoma Entreprise Limitada, from Mozambique, Maripoma Entreprise Limitada, from Ghana, CC Building Limitada and GWIC Moçambique Limitada The largest lot in Inhambane covers the 70-kilometre Sitila–Funhalouro section of road R444, awarded for 2,469,027,132 meticais (€35 million) On the same road corridor, the 40-kilometre Massinga–Sitila section was awarded for 1,612,980,998 meticais (€22.9 million) On national road N222, the 58-kilometre Mapinhane–Macumene section…
